definition_en: A narrow passageway or confined route, especially one running between buildings or through a restricted interior space.
example: Perhaps the smallest suggestion of a moving shadow in the alley.

definition_en: A portable lighting device with a protective enclosure, here powered electrically by LEDs and used to illuminate dark indoor spaces.
example: The LED lantern in hand, Erik finds his way to the fuse box downstairs, located somewhere on the wall behind the staircase.

definition_en: To move repeatedly and rapidly back and forth in small motions, especially when a device produces a silent tactile alert.
example: phone vibrates and lights up

definition_en: To become aware of, perceive, or recognize someone, something, or a fact through observation, attention, or realization.
example: Erik looks up; everyone else keeps moving. Brigid notices this.

definition_en: To give or transfer an object to another person, especially by hand, often so it can continue around a group.
example: He smashes the pig, passes the mallet to Deirdre.

definition_en: To move beyond, alongside, or through the position of a person or place while continuing toward another destination.
example: Deirdre passes Erik and Momo on her way to the bathroom.

definition_en: To cease, disappear, or come to an end with the passage of time, especially a temporary condition, feeling, or difficult period.
example: “This, too, shall pass,” / and I’d roll my eyes at her, but . . .

definition_en: An interior passage in a building that connects rooms, doors, stairways, elevators, or other spaces and allows people to move between them.
example: Richard goes upstairs, opens the upstairs door and waits in the hallway for Momo and Deirdre to get off the elevator.

definition_en: Strange, unusual, or unsettling because it differs noticeably from what is normal, expected, familiar, or socially comfortable.
example: That is the weirdest tradition—

definition_en: A simple fastening device for a door, gate, or similar barrier, released by lifting, sliding, or otherwise moving a catch.
example: “May the Virgin and her Child lift your latch on Christmas night.”

definition_en: In a deliberate, intentional, and purposeful manner, often implying conscious persistence in an action or attitude despite reasons to do otherwise.
example: Initially, I must confess, I found Brigid’s compositions almost willfully opposed to specificity and urgency.

definition_en: Having no windows or other glazed openings that provide outside light, views, or ventilation.
example: DOWNSTAIRS: two windowless rooms divided by an even larger open entryway—with a different floorplan than upstairs.

definition_en: Unsteady or wavering in sound, with noticeable fluctuations in pitch, tone, or intensity rather than a smooth, stable quality.
example: (Going upstairs, wobbly ghost wail)

definition_en: Feeling anxious, uneasy, or concerned about a situation, person, or possible negative outcome.
translations: s'inquiéter | se faire du souci | être inquiet
example: Well I don’t blame you for worrying, especially after—Brigid told me about . . .

definition_en: Mental sharpness, intelligence, or sound judgment, especially the ability to understand situations quickly and act sensibly.
example: And all I’ve done for want of wit,

definition_en: A United States postal code consisting of digits used to identify a geographic area for mail sorting and delivery.
To remove, discard, eliminate, or free oneself from someone or something unwanted or unnecessary.
translations: se débarrasser de | éliminer | se défaire de
example: Hey, why don’t—all right, Lover-Of-All, come on, come with me, let’s get rid of some of this . . .

definition_en: To have the opportunity, privilege, or chance to do something, often implying that the opportunity is valued, limited, or unavailable.
translations: avoir l’occasion de | avoir la chance de | pouvoir
example: I got it, I never get to see her . . .

definition_en: To be required or obliged to do something because circumstances, rules, or practical necessity make it necessary.
example: you gotta take care of yourself.

definition_en: To open a door, window, or similar barrier only a small amount, leaving it partly closed.
example: Brigid cracks the bathroom door open, hands Aimee the toilet paper, then shuts the door.

definition_en: To open a sealed container, especially a bottle or can of a drink, so its contents can be consumed.
translations: ouvrir | décapsuler | ouvrir une canette de
example: Erik cracks open another beer.

definition_en: A person who behaves or speaks in an annoyingly clever, sarcastic, smug, or cheeky way, especially by making pointed remarks.
translations: petit malin | monsieur je-sais-tout | malin | grande gueule
example: Yeah, smart-ass, I’ll give you a fancy candle . . .

definition_en: To be in a satisfactory, safe, healthy, or emotionally stable condition, without serious difficulty or harm.
translations: aller bien | être en état | ça va
example: I’m all right . . .

definition_en: Signals acceptance, acknowledgment, readiness, or a transition to the next action or topic in conversation.
example: All right, let’s just, let’s show Rich how badly our voices blend, / we’ll do the money verses, yeah? . . .

definition_en: Used at the end of an utterance to request confirmation, agreement, or acknowledgment from the listener.
example: I liked you living in Queens, all right?
